posts.text: Dust on the River started as a game, then grew into a novelisation. I love seeing the same world behave differently when the player loses control and the reader takes over. https://samfa12.itch.io/dust-on-the-river #indiedev #GameWriting #IndieGames

A story-driven bushranger game about whether a violent past can ever stay buried. Dust on the River is on itch.io and Google Play — and the novelisation is now on Amazon too. https://samfa12.com/ #IndieGames #AustralianGames

One of the interesting parts of turning Dust on the River into a novel was deciding what had to become internal thought instead of player action. Same story world, completely different tools. https://samfa12.com/ #GameWriting #NovelWriting

I like experimenting with where games live: Dust on the River is available on itch.io and Google Play, while the same world now exists as a novel too. Different audiences, same project. https://samfa12.com/ #IndieGames #BookAdaptation

Making Dust on the River has ended up touching game design, Android release work, trailers, controller support and fiction writing. Small projects have a habit of becoming ecosystems. https://samfa12.com/ #SoloDev #IndieGames

Briarhold is an FPS siege game built around a simple pressure: you cannot defend everything at once. The interesting part is making the player understand which threat matters right now. https://samfa12.com/games/briarhold/ #indiedev #FPSGames #SoloDev

Co-op bugs are wonderfully specific. In one Briarhold test the host could see both players shooting, while the guest could see the host firing but not their own shots. Game networking keeps you humble. https://samfa12.com/games/briarhold/ #GameNetworking #CoopGames

A tiny mobile-control decision can change the whole feel of an FPS. In Briarhold I wanted swipe-to-aim to work almost everywhere on screen, with the movement joystick as the obvious exception. https://samfa12.com/games/briarhold/ #MobileGaming #GameDesign

A design problem I keep coming back to in Briarhold: danger should be communicated before it becomes frustration. If Gate 2 is under pressure, the player should feel that visually, not discover it from a failure screen. https://samfa12.com/games/briarhold/ #GameDesign #IndieGames

Briarhold can be played in the browser as well as tested on Android. I like the idea that a game page can be both the storefront and the doorway straight into the game. https://samfa12.com/games/briarhold/ #BrowserGames #FPSGames

Briarhold Alpha.101 is live for browser + Android testing. It fixes the Mason repair/Strengthen/New Run freeze, improves close-range auto-fire, Wicker pursuit and co-op recovery, and adds better bug diagnostics. https://samfa12.com/games/briarhold/ #indiedev #FPSGames

One useful Briarhold change isn't flashy: optional bug reports can now include bounded game progress and recent errors. Better diagnostics means less guessing when a tester hits a weird freeze. https://samfa12.com/games/briarhold/ #GameTesting #GameDev

I finally wired real browser-play stats into Briarhold's site using Cloudflare request data. It's a small thing, but I like turning a static game page into something that can report how people are actually using it. https://samfa12.com/games/briarhold/ #WebAnalytics #IndieDev

The Last Guard is basically one job description taken too far: you are the last guard on a fortress wall while thousands of orcs advance. Defend the wall. Defend your honour. https://samfa12.itch.io/the-last-guard #IndieGames #HordeSurvival

One reason I enjoy browser games is how little friction there is between 'that looks interesting' and actually playing. The Last Guard is one of my experiments in putting a full siege straight behind a link. https://samfa12.itch.io/the-last-guard #BrowserGames #IndieGames

The Horde started as a ray-tracing tech demo and turned into a useful excuse to experiment with atmosphere, huge enemy counts and how much visual ambition a small project can carry. https://samfa12.itch.io/the-horde #gamedev #RayTracing #IndieGames

What would win: 100 duck-sized horses or one horse-sized duck? I built a simulator because apparently just arguing about it wasn't enough. Reproducible seeded Monte Carlo trials included. https://samfa12.com/apps/what-would-win/ #WebGames #Simulation

What Would Win was a fun modelling problem: the result needs to be silly enough to enjoy, but transparent enough that you can see why the simulation reached it. https://samfa12.com/apps/what-would-win/ #GameDesign #SimulationGames

Simulating thousands of battles is easy compared with explaining one of them clearly. A big part of What Would Win has been turning statistics into a battle story a human can actually follow. https://samfa12.com/apps/what-would-win/ #SimulationGames #GameDesign

Pocket Chordsmith exists because sometimes I want to sketch a chord progression on my phone and get it into the rest of a game-audio workflow without fighting the tool. https://samfa12.com/apps/pocket-chordsmith/ #Songwriting #MusicTech

A web songwriting tool somehow turned into a Godot addon. Pocket Chordsmith can hand song data into game projects for adaptive music workflows — exactly the kind of feature creep I enjoy. https://samfa12.com/apps/pocket-chordsmith/ #godot #GameAudio #Songwriting

The boring part of creative tools is often moving the work between devices. Pocket Audio Handoff exists specifically to make phone → desktop → game-engine transfer less annoying. https://samfa12.com/apps/pocket-audio-handoff/ #MusicTech #GameAudio

I keep coming back to small tools that solve one irritation properly. Pocket Chordsmith is a browser-based songwriting workspace for progressions, MIDI ideas and game-audio handoff. https://samfa12.com/apps/pocket-chordsmith/ #Songwriting #WebAudio

Cursed Cutter is a small browser roguelite experiment: survive cursed waves, choose improvised upgrades, and keep pushing until the run collapses. No install required. https://samfa12.com/games/cursed-cutter/ #Roguelite #BrowserGames

Bug Swarm is a touch-first tower-defense experiment built around fast floods of enemies and deliberately scrappy, handmade-feeling towers. Sometimes a rough visual idea is the whole personality of a game. https://samfa12.com/games/bug-swarm/ #TowerDefense #MobileGames

The Broken Road Trilogy begins 1 October with The Wall that Lied. A fractured road, a city behind stone, and a truth that was never meant to survive. https://samfa12.com/books/ #amwriting #FantasyBooks #IndieAuthor

A character rule I like: Parker would rather run from a fair fight than win one and get hurt. If he draws a sword, he has already tried to tilt the odds first. That idea shaped a lot of The Broken Road Trilogy. https://samfa12.com/books/ #FantasyBooks #CharacterWriting

Parker isn't a chosen hero. He's a council officer dealing with roads, bridges and engineering in a place that would rather forget him. That mundane job became a useful way into a much bigger story. https://samfa12.com/books/ #FantasyBooks #Worldbuilding

One thing I enjoy in siege stories is competence without invincibility. People can make smart decisions, prepare well, and still lose something important. That tension sits underneath The Broken Road Trilogy. https://samfa12.com/books/ #FantasyWriting #SiegeFiction
The Broken Road Trilogy is being released one month at a time: The Wall that Lied on 1 Oct, No Wall to Hold on 1 Nov, and What We Save on 1 Dec. https://samfa12.com/books/ #FantasyBooks #BookSeries

The Broken Road books started with walls, roads and engineering, but the question underneath them became more interesting: what are people actually trying to preserve when a city is under pressure? https://samfa12.com/books/ #FantasyWriting #Worldbuilding

samfa12.com has gradually become less of a portfolio and more of a launchpad: books, games, browser experiments, music tools and the odd idea that probably should have stayed a thought experiment. https://samfa12.com/ #IndieDev #IndieAuthor

I still like how far a mostly static website can go. samfa12.com is GitHub Pages underneath, but it now hosts playable games, tools, release pages and automated analytics. https://samfa12.com/ #webdev #GitHubPages #IndieDev

My projects have a habit of bleeding into each other: a game becomes a novel, a songwriting tool becomes a Godot addon, a silly argument becomes a simulator. Honestly, that's half the fun. https://samfa12.com/ #CreativeCoding #IndieAuthor
I like building things that are small enough to finish but strange enough to be memorable: games, books, browser tools, experiments. The full pile is here: https://samfa12.com/ #IndieDev #IndieAuthor

I automated my tiny marketing pipeline: a curated content bank lives in GitHub, a weekly Action schedules ten X posts into Buffer across seven days, and Buffer publishes them on cue. Less admin, more time making things. https://samfa12.com/ #BuildInPublic #MarketingAutomation

Pocket Pattern is live on itch.io: shake a 3×3 target, slide chunky tiles until the centre matches, then chase a faster time or fewer moves. Touch-first, browser-based, with music made in Pocket Chordsmith. https://samfa12.itch.io/pocket-pattern #PuzzleGames #BrowserGames

Pocket Chordsmith v68 makes big WAV exports safer: it checks whether an export is too large for the device before starting, then moves rendering off the main UI where possible. Less flashy; nicer to use. https://samfa12.com/apps/pocket-chordsmith/ #MusicTech #WebAudio

I rebuilt the Samfa12 catalogue around sourced static pages: games, books and tools now get canonical pages, structured metadata and source-backed claims. Less flashy than a new game, but better foundations for a growing project pile. https://samfa12.com/ #WebDev #StaticSite

Backwater is a post-collapse novel about water, survival and control. Its itch.io vertical slice turns that same pressure into play. I keep finding excuses to let stories escape their original medium. https://samfa12.com/books/backwater/ #PostApocalyptic #SurvivalFiction

Drink ends where honesty begins. Sober picks up six months later and follows what change costs after the dramatic moment. The game and novel share a world without trying to be the same thing. https://samfa12.com/books/sober/ #IndieAuthor #ContemporaryFiction

Colossal is my Roman tragedy about an enslaved gladiator who turns fame into a weapon. I wanted the arena spectacle to matter less than what happens when a person becomes valuable to people who still own him. https://samfa12.com/books/colossal/ #HistoricalFiction #IndieAuthor

ToKnight starts with an ordinary Year 6 kid, a mysterious inheritance, and a fantasy world that won’t stay separate from school life. Book two, The Fire Beneath, digs deeper into that collision. https://samfa12.com/books/toknight/ #MiddleGrade #FantasyBooks

Free to a Good Home and A Place of His Own are connected novels about care, belonging, family pressure and independence. No magic or apocalypse—just people trying to do the right thing when right isn’t easy. https://samfa12.com/books/ #ContemporaryFiction #IndieAuthor

Concubine is political science fiction about occupation, personhood, resistance, faith and control. It’s less interested in heroes than in what power does to people forced to live inside it. https://samfa12.com/books/concubine/ #SciFiBooks #DystopianFiction

Article 18 is a speculative-noir novella I put in more than one form: ebook/PDF on itch.io, plus ebook and audiobook on Google Play. Sometimes a small story is a good excuse to experiment with how readers find it. https://samfa12.com/books/article-18/ #NoirFiction #Audiobooks

Breakfast Beat began with a specific idea: what if a tower-defense board was also a musical sequencer? Lanes form chords, columns fire on beats, and your breakfast defences build the groove as they fight. https://samfa12.itch.io/breakfast-beat #TowerDefense #GameMusic

Wonky Vehicle Lab lets you draw a questionable vehicle, glue or weld it together, then ask physics for a second opinion. You can even share builds as WVL1 codes. If it falls apart immediately, that is research. https://samfa12.itch.io/wonky-vehicle-lab #PhysicsGames #IndieGames

Mandible Wars squeezes an RTS-lite into portrait phone play: ants vs termites, fog of war, base building, strongpoints and two victory modes. I wanted to see how much real RTS feeling could fit under one thumb. https://samfa12.itch.io/mandible-wars #RTSGames #MobileGaming

Moon Mower is exactly what it sounds like: a tiny astronaut mowing glowing grass on a spherical moon while rescuing trapped spirits. It’s my favourite kind of project—a joke premise that becomes genuinely relaxing. https://samfa12.itch.io/moon-mower #CozyGames #IndieGames

Spin Vector uses Pocket Chordsmith song data inside the game: ten neon arenas, twin-stick combat, persistent upgrades and adaptive music that follows the level mechanics instead of simply sitting behind them. https://samfa12.itch.io/spin-vector #TwinStickShooter #AdaptiveMusic

Reckless Dentist is my answer to a question nobody asked: can drag-and-drop dental work become a frantic score-attack game? Clean, fill and yank the right tooth before the clinic becomes complete nonsense. https://samfa12.itch.io/reckless-dentist #ArcadeGames #BrowserGames

Pocket Ant Farm is a living voxel colony: watch ants dig, drop food, nudge tunnel growth, and make the dirt transparent to peek inside. There’s no grand victory condition—just a tiny system that’s pleasant to watch. https://samfa12.itch.io/ant-farm #SimulationGames #CozyGames

The Wall that Lied is now published on Amazon. Book 1 of The Broken Road opens with Tomas Parker: an engineer, a hated saviour, and the man Auster needs again when its defences may rest on a lie. https://samfa12.com/books/the-wall-that-lied/ #fantasy #IndieAuthor #FantasyBooks

Briarhold Alpha.102 is ready for browser + Android testing. Ashwing is clearer and targetable, dive/ash warnings are easier to read, fortress presentation is improved, and stability testing continues. https://samfa12.com/games/briarhold/ #FPSGames #IndieDev

Breakfast Beat-down: Rush Hour Remix v0.2 is playable now. Fight breakfast waves with a spatula, time attacks to beat/offbeat/melody cues, build Groove, and buy permanent Pantry upgrades between runs. https://samfa12.com/games/breakfast-beat-down/ #RhythmGame #Roguelite

Night Shift at Possum's Café is a cosy little service game: play a possum barista, serve animal customers, manage short rushes, and keep the warm night café moving. It’s live on itch.io and Google Play. https://samfa12.itch.io/possum-cafe #CozyGames #MobileGaming

Pocket Fish Tank is a small low-poly aquarium world built around fish-care progression and a calm ambient loop. It’s playable on itch.io and also lives inside the Samfa12 Lofi and Chill Pack on Android. https://samfa12.itch.io/fish-tank #CozyGames #IndieGames

The Horde 1.6.2 is live for Windows and Android. Its graphics preview lets you compare ray-traced water, fire, glass, mist and dust before keeping a setting—useful when every GPU has a different comfort zone. https://samfa12.com/games/the-horde/ #RayTracing #GameDev

In Banana Banana Ducky!, every duck you hug puts on a red tie and helps recruit the rest. v1.1 has four playable worlds, touch controls and character swapping—including becoming one of your own flock. https://samfa12.com/games/banana-banana-ducky/ #BrowserGames #IndieGames

Pocket DAW is the desktop half of a phone-to-game-audio workflow: import Pocket Chordsmith songs, edit audio and MIDI on a timeline, then export WAV, MIDI, stems or a game-audio manifest. https://samfa12.itch.io/pocket-daw #MusicTech #GameAudio

Pocket Chordsmith is the studio; Pocket DJ is the stage. Import a song, launch its sections from performance pads, mute stems, loop bars, build tension and drop back into the groove—all in a mobile-friendly browser deck. https://samfa12.itch.io/pocket-dj #MusicTech #WebAudio

P.A.R.T.Y. Bus sends a battered yellow bus down the Rust Mile for scrap, fuel and survivors. The real decision is when to turn back before damage, weight, enemies or optimism make the return trip impossible. https://samfa12.itch.io/party-bus #SurvivalGames #BrowserGames

Gremlin Grenade Pinball is a prototype where the ball is a live grenade and gremlins crawl across the table. Keep it alive with the flippers, hit trap targets and time explosions before the horde breaks through. https://samfa12.itch.io/gremlin-grenade-pinball #Pinball #IndieGames

Bug Maze TD poses a neat tower-defence problem: ground bugs must path around the maze you build, while flying enemies ignore it. Four phone-friendly levels add hazards, hero bugs and water-only towers. https://samfa12.itch.io/bug-maze-td #TowerDefense #MobileGaming

Hop Bunny turns one button into a precision challenge: hold to charge, release to chase the target height, then scale from tiny centimetre hops to a final launch toward the carrot moon. https://samfa12.itch.io/hop-bunny #ArcadeGames #BrowserGames

Ship Blockade compresses tower defence into a narrow shipping lane: place patrol guns, mines, missile batteries and blocker boats while faster skiffs, armoured tankers and support ships keep changing the pressure. https://samfa12.itch.io/ship-blockade #TowerDefense #BrowserGames
